about: Curated lists for the ✨ Originality check (originality.py). Phrases are matched as whole words, case-insensitive, with straight or curly apostrophes. In a phrase, {pron} matches he/she/they/I/we/you, {poss} his/her/their/my/our/your, {obj} him/her/them/me/us/you, {be} was/were/is/are/am, and a word ending in * matches any ending (delv* = delve, delves, delved, delving). Each item is a phrase, or [phrase, reason]; without a reason the group's reason is used. Edit this file to add your own.

ai_phrases.label: Phrase that sounds machine-written
ai_phrases.why: This phrase turns up again and again in AI-written fiction; readers who have seen it before stop trusting the page.
ai_phrases.advice: Say the plain thing, or show the one concrete detail this phrase stands in for.
items: “A testament to” is a stock AI phrase: it tells the reader what something proves instead of letting them see it.
“Tapestry” as a metaphor (a tapestry of sounds, lives, cultures) is one of the best-known AI tells.
“Delve” is a word AI writers use far more often than people do.
“The weight of …” (her words, his gaze, the silence) is a stock AI way to make a feeling sound heavy without showing it.
“The weight of the …” is a stock AI way to make a feeling sound heavy without showing it.
“The weight of it all” names a feeling instead of showing it.
“Couldn't help but …” is filler that AI uses to soften an action; just say what they did.
“Could not help but …” is filler that AI uses to soften an action; just say what they did.
“A symphony of …” (smells, sounds, colours) is a stock AI flourish.
“A cacophony of …” is a stock AI flourish for noise.
“A kaleidoscope of …” is a stock AI flourish for colour.
“A dance of …” (light, shadows, flames) is a stock AI image.
“Little did they know” is an old cliché that AI loves; it gives away the surprise.
“A breath she didn't know she was holding” is the most famous AI and fan-fiction cliché.
“A breath he hadn't known he was holding” is the most famous AI and fan-fiction cliché.
“A breath they didn't realize they were holding” is a famous cliché.
“Sent shivers down her spine” is a stock reaction; show what the body really did.
“Sent a shiver down his spine” is a stock reaction; show what the body really did.
“A shiver ran down her spine” is a stock reaction; show what the body really did.
in the grand scheme of things
“In the grand scheme of things” is filler that AI uses to sound wise.
“It's important to note” is essay language, not story language; it sounds like a chatbot.
“It is important to note” is essay language, not story language; it sounds like a chatbot.
“It's worth noting” is essay language that sounds like a chatbot.
“Navigate the complexities” is corporate AI language.
“The complexities of …” is vague AI language; name the actual problem.
“An intricate dance” is a stock AI image.
“Intricate” is one of the words AI writers overuse; is there a more exact word?
“Palpable” (the tension was palpable) is a stock AI word that tells instead of shows.
“The air was thick with …” is a stock AI opening for atmosphere.
“The air thick with …” is a stock AI opening for atmosphere.
“Hung heavy in the air” is a stock AI phrase.
“Hung in the air” (words, silence, a question) is a stock AI phrase.
“A mix of fear and hope” (two feelings at once) is a habit of AI prose that names feelings instead of showing them.
“A mixture of …” feelings names them instead of showing them, a habit of AI prose.
“A sense of …” (dread, purpose, wonder) is a vague AI way to name a feeling.
“A flicker of …” (hope, doubt, recognition) is a stock AI way to name a feeling.
“A pang of …” is a stock way to name a feeling.
“A wave of …” (relief, nausea, emotion) is a stock way to name a feeling.
“… washed over her” is a stock AI phrase for a feeling.
“A beacon of hope” is a stock AI phrase.
“Beacon of hope” is a stock AI phrase.
“An unspoken understanding” is a stock AI phrase; show the look or the gesture.
“A silent understanding” is a stock AI phrase; show the look or the gesture.
“The silence was deafening” is a cliché.
“An eternity” (for a pause) is a stock exaggeration.
“What felt like an eternity” is a stock AI phrase for a pause.
“Time seemed to stand still” is a cliché.
“In that moment” is a filler phrase AI uses to sound dramatic.
“Something deep within” is vague AI language; say what the character felt or did.
“Deep down” is vague; show the feeling instead.
“The ghost of a smile” is a stock AI phrase.
“A smile tugged at the corner of her mouth” is a stock AI phrase.
tugged at the corners of {poss} mouth
“Tugged at the corners of his mouth” is a stock AI phrase.
“Eyes sparkling with …” is a stock AI phrase.
“Eyes that held …” (a thousand stories, a secret) is a stock AI phrase.
“A thousand stories” is a stock AI phrase.
“Whispered promises” is a stock AI phrase.
“A reminder that …” tells the reader the lesson; let the scene make the point.
“A stark reminder” tells the reader the lesson; let the scene make the point.
“A poignant reminder” tells the reader the lesson; let the scene make the point.
“Poignant” tells the reader how to feel; AI uses it a lot.
“Bittersweet” names a mixed feeling instead of showing it; AI uses it a lot.
“Profound” tells the reader something matters; AI uses it a lot.
“Resilience” is an abstract word AI uses to sum up a character; show what they endured.
“Indomitable” is an AI favourite for summing up a character.
“Unwavering” (resolve, gaze, loyalty) is an AI favourite.
“Newfound” (courage, confidence) is an AI favourite; it announces growth instead of showing it.
“Embark on a journey” is stock AI language.
“A journey of self-discovery” is stock AI language.
“Uncharted territory” is a stock AI phrase.
“The fabric of …” (reality, society) is a stock AI metaphor.
“The very fabric” is a stock AI metaphor.
“… echoed through the halls/room/night” is a stock AI image.
“A stark contrast” is essay language that AI drops into stories.
“In stark contrast” is essay language that AI drops into stories.
“Nestled” (a village nestled in the hills) is a word AI uses far too often.
“Bustling” (a bustling market) is a word AI uses far too often.
“Vibrant” is a word AI uses far too often; name the colour or the noise.
“Ethereal” is an AI favourite; what does it actually look like?
“Otherworldly” is an AI favourite; what does it actually look like?
“Testament” (a testament to her skill) is one of the best-known AI words.
“A whirlwind of …” is a stock AI phrase.
“A maelstrom of …” (emotions) is a stock AI phrase.
“A torrent of …” (emotions, words) is a stock AI phrase.
“A storm of emotions” names feelings instead of showing them.
“Every fibre of her being” is a stock AI exaggeration.
“Every fibre of his being” is a stock AI exaggeration.
“Her heart pounded in her chest” is a stock AI reaction.
“His heart hammered” is a stock AI reaction.
“A mischievous glint” is a stock AI phrase.
“A glint in her eye” is a stock AI phrase.
“The promise of …” (rain, adventure) is a stock AI phrase.
“Whispers of …” (the past, the wind) is a stock AI phrase.
“The dance of …” (light, shadows) is a stock AI image.
“… danced across her face/the walls” is a stock AI image.
“A lifetime ago” is a stock phrase.
“A world away” is a stock phrase.
“The world seemed to …” (hold its breath, fall away) is a stock AI phrase.
“The world held its breath” is a stock AI phrase.
“… held its breath” (the room, the city) is a stock AI image.
“As if the universe …” is a stock AI flourish.
“Somewhere deep inside” is vague; show the feeling.
“A quiet strength” is an AI favourite for summing up a character.
“Quiet determination” is an AI favourite for summing up a character.
“A reminder of …” tells the reader what to think; let the detail do it.
“More than just a …” is a stock AI way to make something sound important.
“Only time would tell” is a cliché.
“The journey ahead” is stock AI language for an ending.
“Whatever the future held” is stock AI language for an ending.
“Whatever came next” is stock AI language for an ending.

cliches.label: Cliché
cliches.why: A worn-out phrase: readers have seen it so often that it no longer makes a picture.
cliches.advice: Replace it with something only this character, in this place, would see or say.
items: at the end of the day
every cloud has a silver lining
it was a dark and stormy night
like a moth to a flame
plenty of fish in the sea
the light at the end of the tunnel
in the blink of an eye
to make a long story short
a force to be reckoned with

hedges.label: Too much hedging
hedges.why: The narration keeps softening itself (perhaps, somehow, seemed, as if); AI prose hedges like this to avoid committing to anything.
hedges.advice: Commit: say what happened. Keep a hedge only where the character truly cannot know.

thresholds.about: per 1 000 words of narration (dialogue is not counted unless asked): minor at or above 'minor', major at or above 'major'; 'min' hits before anything is said

writer_brief.about: What the chapter writer is told BEFORE it writes (human_voice.py, the brief's human_voice block): the first 'take' phrases of each list above (they are in order, best-known first) plus 'always', shown with she/her/was for the placeholders ('show' gives a phrase's display form), the patterns to never write and the craft rules. 'gestures' is the body-language list the cross-chapter repeat check counts. Edit this to change what every new chapter is told.
patterns: “Not X. Not Y.” lists of what something is not
“It wasn't X. It was Y.” (say what it is, straight away)
lists of three (“cold, wet, and tired”) again and again: at most one in a scene; write a pair (“cold and wet”) or one exact detail (“her socks squelched at every step”) instead
a paragraph or scene that ends on a moral or a big truth about life
long dashes (—) in most paragraphs: use full stops and commas
hedging (perhaps, somehow, seemed to, as if) in sentence after sentence
questions the narrator asks the reader (“What did it mean?”)
naming a feeling right after showing it (“Her hands shook. She was afraid.”)
craft: Vary sentence length: mix short, blunt sentences with longer ones; never three of the same length in a row.
Use concrete details only this story could have (a name, a smell, a brand, a worn object), not generic ones.
Leave subtext: show the feeling through action and what people avoid saying; never name it afterwards.
Make dialogue messy and real: people interrupt, dodge questions, answer the wrong thing, trail off.
End scenes on an action or an image, never on a lesson or a summary.
Do not repeat a gesture or a description from earlier chapters (jaws, breaths, nods, glances).
gestures: pressed {poss} lips into a thin line
